mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 consecutive months prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in consumer confidence (HOUST) weakens wage growth expectations, causing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND HOUST < previous month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with weak sentiment
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to a baseline of stable labor and sentiment (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 on the decision date indicates strengthening supply-side momentum that translates into higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with INDPRO spikes (Spearman rho < 0.2, p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days as investors anticipate tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% surprise in the month before decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during prior high-inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining unemployment (UNRATE) and rising retail sales (implied via HOUST) suggest a labor market softening that supports rate cuts, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous month for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST > previous month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with improving retail activity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than during comparable softening cycles (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in consumer spending (HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as earnings growth expectations cool.
regime_hint: labor market contraction with stagnant consumer demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with payroll declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the manufacturing component of industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double-digit month-over-month increase, it signals supply chain acceleration that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during typical supply expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stable federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns as market expectations shift toward rate stability and easing inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 4% for the prior 2 months
regime_hint: low inflation and stable policy environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during high-inflation/variable-rate periods (p < 0.05).
